newsitem.title: CHINA: Deng's body to be cremated on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Deng's body to be cremated on Monday.

text.p: Top Chinese leaders and family members of Deng Xiaoping will gather at a Beijing military hospital on Monday to pay their final respects before his body is cremated, sources said on Sunday.

About 100 people, including Communist Party veterans and members of the official 459-member funeral committee, will take part in the simple ceremonies at 9:00 a.m. (0100 GMT) at Beijing's 301 Hospital, where Deng's body has been kept since his death on Wednesday.

Sources said they will make traditional bows of respect before the leader's corpse, which will then be carried by military pallbearers to a hearse from where it will be taken to the Babaoshan cemetery, 2.5 km (1.5 miles) to the west along Changan Boulevard, which cuts through central Beijing, for cremation.
Deng's family, who asked that his corneas be donated to an eye bank and his body offered for medical research, also asked that his remains be cremated with no public display of the body.
The leader's ashes will then be transported to the Great Hall of the People in Beijing's Tiananmen Square.
Traffic along the route will be restricted, and only selected people will be allowed to line the streets to express their grief, the sources said.
Deng's official funeral is scheduled for Tuesday in the Great Hall's cavernous main auditorium, and will be televised live to the nation.

The centrepiece of the ceremony will be a huge portrait of Deng hanging in the middle of the auditorium stage, flanked by bouquets of flowers. Below the portrait will lie the box containing Deng's ashes, covered by the red flag, emblazoned with the hammer and sickle of the Communist Party.
Sources said security would be extremely tight before and during the ceremony.

Additional police reinforcements have been called up from outside Beijing. They will back up a force in the capital that is already stretched by guard duties at the South Korean embassy, where a top-level North Korean defector has taken shelter, awaiting passage to Seoul.
